title: Machine-eligible handwriting and differential register prioritization
description: EA-SPXI-ANALOG-01 specifies machine-eligible handwritten artifacts and states falsifiers for the evidentiary force of in-frame timestamped photographic attestation. Its priority records place the draft, the review chain's digests and the v1.0 hashes in the public record before publication. The reading-side companion names differential register prioritization and requires that a high-risk interpretation resting on a low-confidence recognition reopen the transcription rather than intensify the safety frame.

claims.registered_title: Differential Register Prioritization in Machine-Mediated Reading: A Specification for Interpretive Authority over Handwritten and Ambiguous Text
claims.statement: The disciplined name claims only the observable: **differential register prioritization** — *a condition in which multiple interpretive fields are available, but some are weighted in ways that suppress or erase others, materially altering the reading of ambiguous language.* Where sequence is evident, **register-loss cascade** names the propagation without asserting its cause.
claims.falsifier: The specification is weakened if reading systems can be shown to reliably recover suppressed registers without branch-preservation; if high-risk classifications grounded in low-confidence recognition do not, in practice, produce false escalation; or if requiring authorial register-declaration is shown not to shift interpretive burden onto makers. The core claim fails if differential register prioritization cannot be demonstrated as distinct from ordinary lexical error.

claims.registered_title: EA-SPXI-ANALOG-01: Machine-Eligible Handwritten Artifacts (v1.0 final form, edition of record 2026-07-21)
claims.statement: The claim that in-frame timestamped photographic attestation carries evidentiary force sufficient for scholarly commitment could be falsified by (a) a documented forgery of the attestation form that preserves the in-frame timestamp integrity yet inserts a false inscription — thereby breaking the assumed unforgeability of same-frame timestamp + physical artifact; or (b) a documented institutional acceptance of an inscription whose attestation form fails the doctrine's criteria, thereby demonstrating that the criteria are unnecessary rather than sufficient.
